risk_profiles.content: ETH+ is collateralized by LSTs (currently wstETH, weETH, rETH, sfrxETH, ETHx) held in Reserve Protocol smart contracts with no external custodians. Effective collateralization is approximately 102%, and approximately 0.25% of ETH+ market cap providing mechanistic first-loss capital. Holders have redemption autonomy at the protocol layer, but not contractual redemption rights.

Decentralized. Governance operates through on-chain RSR staker voting with a 72-hour execution delay and an approximate eight-day end-to-end cycle. Five roles are defined: owner, pauser, short freezer, long freezer, and guardian. No role can directly mint, seize user funds, or upgrade logic outside the timelocked process. Freeze roles are time-limited and self-consuming; the guardian may veto but not initiate actions. No formal incident response playbook has been published, though the March 2023 USDC depeg event on sibling RTokens demonstrated the recollateralization mechanism performing as designed under live stress. Guardian signer composition and threshold are not published in narrative documentation and require direct on-chain inspection.

ETH+ recorded annualized price volatility of approximately 18.4% over the trailing year, against ETH. The LST-basket-to-ETH exchange rate registered no material deviations over the same period. Thirty-day average secondary trading volume exceeds $1M daily.

Reserve Protocol has undergone approximately nine core audit engagements including Trail of Bits, Code4rena, Halborn, Solidified, Ackee Blockchain, Trust Security, and Oak Security (March 2026), with no critical findings reaching production. A $10M Immunefi bug bounty is active across core contracts and LST collateral plugins. No security incident has affected bsdETH or Reserve Protocol since the October 2022 mainnet launch. The primary residual gap is the absence of full formal mathematical verification.

All reserves are held on-chain and verifiable in real time with no reliance on attestations or third-party reporting. Basket rebalancing is executed through on-chain governance with Dutch auction settlement. Approximately 90% of staking yield accrues to ETH+ holders; of the remaining 10%, 3% flows to staked RSR and 7% to RSR buy-and-burn. In a collateral default event, staked RSR is mechanistically seized and auctioned on-chain without requiring a governance vote; unstaking carries a mandatory 14-day delay. Redemptions are permissionless at T+0, subject to an hourly throttle, and remain available even when issuance is paused.

No entity holds reserves on behalf of holders; LST collateral sits in on-chain smart contracts that mechanically enforce redemption, with no human counterparty to claim against. LST-issuer custody risk is captured in the Asset Quality section.

tBTC is fully collateralized by native Bitcoin against its circulating supply, with no leverage and no other reserve assets. BTC is held in Bitcoin addresses whose private keys are split across 100 independent node operators, with 51 required to authorize any transaction. The principal constraints are the absence of contractual redemption rights for holders and the operational security of key share management across a distributed operator set.

Semi-centralized. Governance is nominally decentralized through T token holder voting, but in practice centralized: votes are conducted off-chain via Snapshot and are non-binding, leaving an elected 6-of-9 council as the sole on-chain execution authority for all upgrades and parameter changes. The council operates under a 48-hour timelock and cannot seize or blacklist user funds. No formal incident response playbook exists.

tBTC maintains its 1:1 BTC peg through supply constraint: every token requires a verified BTC deposit and is redeemable for 1 BTC minus 0.2%. Annualized volatility has remained in the 0–5% band with effectively zero days of material deviation. Thirty-day average volume exceeds $1 million, price history for tBTC v2 tracks back to late 2022.

The sole independent core audit was conducted by Least Authority in September 2022; all subsequent core audits have been performed by an affiliated firm, creating a meaningful independence concern. No formal verification exists. An active bug bounty has paid $638,900 to date against a $150,000 critical maximum.

Reserves are native Bitcoin held across distributed operator wallets, fully verifiable on-chain in real time with no attestation dependency. Redemptions process in approximately 3–5 hours but carry no contractual guarantee; an October 2023 bug temporarily blocked all redemptions before being patched within days.

No entity holds reserves on behalf of holders; BTC sits across 100 independent node operators with redemption enforced by threshold signatures, and no human counterparty to claim against. Operator key-share security is captured in the Asset Quality section.

stETH maintains a 1:1 collateralization ratio against ETH held natively on the Ethereum Beacon Chain. The Lido insurance fund provides only negligible first-loss coverage relative to TVL. Disbursement requires a DAO governance vote with no automatic trigger.

Decentralized. Lido DAO governs via Aragon, with contract upgrades executed by the Aragon Agent smart contract following a successful LDO vote (5% quorum, simple majority) and a minimum 4-day delay before execution; no human multisig sits in the execution path. Dual Governance, deployed July 2025, grants stETH holders veto rights: opposition above 1% of supply extends delays by 5–45 days; above 10%, governance suspends entirely via Rage Quit. Validator operations remain concentrated, with the Curated Module accounting for ~92% of staked ETH, and on-chain participation structurally low.

stETH is designed to track ETH 1:1. Over the trailing 365 days, annualized volatility versus ETH stood at around 2%, with zero trading days recording a deviation exceeding 1%. The most notable stress event in the period was a ~0.3% deviation in July 2025, driven by a surge in the validator withdrawal queue following a large leveraged-unwind episode. 30-day average trading volume exceeds $1 million.

Lido has undergone 90+ independent security reviews on Ethereum mainnet, with formal verification completed by Certora (V2 and Dual Governance modules) and Runtime Verification (Dual Governance mechanism design). The most recent formal verification engagement concluded in February 2025, placing audit recency at the maximum tier. All identified critical and high-severity findings were remediated prior to deployment. A $2M maximum Immunefi bug bounty covers core contracts. Contract maturity exceeds 60 months with no material exploit recorded.

ETH backing stETH is held natively on the Ethereum Beacon Chain and is verifiable on-chain in real time against circulating stETH supply without reliance on third-party attestation or off-chain reporting. No external custodian is involved. Reserve management is entirely passive: deposited ETH is delegated to Lidos curated node operator set with no active trading, rehypothecation, or yield optimization applied to principal.

No entity holds reserves on behalf of holders; ETH sits natively on the Ethereum Beacon Chain, with no human counterparty to claim against. The Samuels v. Lido DAO lawsuit is a residual legal-classification risk against the LDO token, not stETH holders.

rETH is backed by natively staked ETH held at a healthy overcollateralization margin, with the exchange rate designed to rise monotonically as staking, priority-fee, and MEV rewards accrue. Node operators post first-loss ETH and token collateral ahead of rETH holders, and there is no external custodian, removing a common source of counterparty risk for this asset class. Overall credit quality is strong, though it is somewhat tempered by rETH's smaller scale relative to the largest liquid staking tokens and the absence of a dedicated external insurance fund.

Rocket Pool operates a dual-DAO structure: a token-voted protocol DAO that sets parameters and treasury policy, and a permissioned oracle council of roughly nine to sixteen trusted node operators that executes contract upgrades under a majority-consensus threshold. Roles, addresses, and upgrade procedures are extensively documented, and a single centralized guardian key is being phased out in favor of broader council control, which is a notable strength. The upgrade threshold remains a relatively modest majority of a small council, and no formally published incident-response playbook exists, which warrants monitoring.

rETH's exchange rate against ETH has a well-established track record exceeding one year, with only a small share of trading days showing any meaningful deviation from expected value. Secondary market liquidity is maintained across numerous exchanges and decentralized venues, though trading volumes are more modest than those of the largest liquid staking tokens, which constrains the depth of the track record somewhat. No material peg-stability concerns have been identified to date.

Rocket Pool's core contracts have undergone 11 independent audits across six security firms since 2021, representing roughly $500,000 in cumulative audit spend, with the most recent reviews (Cantina and Bailsec) completed in late 2025 and early 2026 ahead of the Saturn 1 upgrade. A critical reentrancy vulnerability was identified by ConsenSys Diligence during the 2023 Atlas audit and remediated with a dedicated guard before it could affect users, and no exploit has touched user funds across more than 53 months of mainnet operation. An Immunefi bug bounty currently caps critical-severity payouts at $150,000, down from $500,000 as of February 2026, and the protocol relies on manual review, static analysis, and fuzzing rather than formal verification, marking the main gap relative to top-tier liquid staking peers.

All reserves backing rETH consist of ETH staked on Ethereum's consensus layer plus execution-layer liquidity, held entirely within protocol smart contracts that are non-upgradable for core custody functions. Backing is continuously and independently verifiable on-chain without reliance on third-party attestations or periodic reporting, a notable strength relative to off-chain reserve models. There is no dedicated external insurance fund beyond the first-loss capital posted by individual node operators.

The issuing entity does not currently hold financial or stablecoin-specific regulatory licenses, and neither the issuer nor the on-chain custody arrangement benefits from formal bankruptcy-remoteness structures such as a special-purpose vehicle or trust. In practice, counterparty exposure is mitigated because assets are held directly in immutable smart contracts rather than by a custodian, though redemption rights, asset segregation, and beneficial-ownership provisions are not explicitly addressed in the protocol's public terms, representing a structural gap for institutional users seeking contractual clarity.

Holder concentration is low, by the widest margin of any asset in the assessed pool. The post-filter index sits far inside the least concentrated tiering band for its class. Unlike comparable derivatives, the substantial majority of supply is held in ordinary wallets rather than in lending, restaking or bridge contracts, so the measured base is broadly representative of true ownership, and the issuer holds no inventory. The tier assignment is stable under every reading and sensitivity tested. Concentration is not a material risk driver for this asset.

No security incident, exploit, or fund loss has affected rETH or the Rocket Pool protocol within the past six months, extending a clean operational track record spanning more than four years of mainnet activity. A historical non-protocol social media account compromise did not involve any loss of user funds.

Rocket Pool's core contracts have been reviewed in eight dedicated audits (eleven including governance-specific reviews) by six independent security firms, with the most recent reviews completed within the past several months of major protocol upgrades. A live bug bounty offers up to $150,000 for critical vulnerabilities, a reduction from a prior $500,000 ceiling, and the protocol has over four years of mainnet operation with a single historical critical vulnerability identified and remediated well before the current architecture. The principal residual gap is the absence of formal mathematical verification of contract correctness, relying instead on manual review, static analysis, and fuzzing.

eETH is fully backed 1:1 by native ETH staked across Ether.fi's validator set, held entirely in Ether.fi smart contracts with no external custodian. Reserves are independently verifiable in real time on the Ethereum beacon chain and via the LiquidityPool contract, with a Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves feed live since April 2025. Restaking exposure is being wound down. No dedicated insurance fund or equity buffer exists above par.

Semi-centralized. Control splits across two Safe multisigs: a 6-of-10 Upgrade Admin behind a 10-day timelock covering all upgrades, during which proposed code is visible on-chain and dissenting depositors can exit before it ships, and a 4-of-7 Operating Admin with immediate emergency pause and a 2-day parameter timelock that cannot upgrade contracts, alter the oracle, or touch user balances. There is no centralized mint: eETH is minted permissionlessly 1:1 against deposited ETH on mainnet. Every threshold, Safe, and timelock is verifiable on Etherscan, with only signer identities withheld for security. Token-holder voting runs off-chain via ETHFI Snapshot with the Ether.fi Foundation executing outcomes.

eETH targets a 1:1 claim on pooled ETH, with holder balances rebasing daily as consensus and execution-layer rewards accrue rather than the token appreciating in price. Annualized volatility against ETH sits at approximately 2.47% over the trailing 365 days, with no material deviations of note and price history exceeding 365 days. The peg is enforced mechanically by permissionless mint at par and by instant withdrawals. Direct eETH secondary depth is thin and price discovery concentrates at the weETH layer.

eETH is a rebasing ERC-20 of modest complexity, but the underlying Ether.fi protocol is architecturally complex. Core contracts have undergone 11 audits across 8 independent firms, 7 of them scoped specifically to core protocol contracts, complemented by 16 dated Certora formal-verification reports spanning 2024 to 2026, with a core-contracts re-audit completed by Certora in January 2026 and a July 2026 upgrade that compiled key safety guarantees into immutable contract-level invariants under Certora review. A $500K Immunefi bug bounty is active as of July 2026. No smart contract exploit or material loss event has been recorded.

All backing is held as ETH staked on the Ethereum Beacon Chain, verifiable in real time via the LiquidityPool contract without reliance on attestations or third-party auditor reports, supplemented by a Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves feed since April 2025, RedStone corroborating price feeds, and independent DefiLlama TVL tracking. Reserve management is passive, with no rehypothecation or active yield optimization applied to principal. Instant withdrawals are served from an on-chain liquidity buffer with the validator exit queue as fallback, typically settling in 7 to 14 days at full NAV. The mechanism has been tested under live stress: 542,792 ETH, roughly 19.6% of TVL, was redeemed over 33 days during the April 2026 market-wide exit rush with no missed withdrawal and no lengthening of Ethereum's shared exit queue. No dedicated insurance fund or equity buffer exists.

No entity holds reserves on behalf of holders; ETH sits natively on the Ethereum Beacon Chain in protocol smart contracts that enforce redemption on-chain, with no human counterparty to claim against. The dependency on Ether.fi's privileged roles is captured in the Governance section.

Holder concentration is low on a look-through basis but structurally distorted on the raw measure. eETH has roughly 160,000 holder addresses, yet close to 96% of supply sits in the weETH wrapper contract, an architectural artifact of rebasing balances being incompatible with most DeFi venues rather than a beneficial position. Unwrapped eETH float sits below 4% of supply, so direct eETH secondary markets are shallow and exit pressure routes through the wrapper or the protocol redemption channel rather than through open-market sale.
No exploit, fund loss, or smart contract vulnerability has affected eETH or Ether.fi's core contracts within the past six months, or at any point across roughly 35 months of operation.

Reserves are held equally across wstETH, cbETH, and wsuperOETHb in Reserve Protocol smart contracts on Base, with 100% collateralization enforced by design. 0.25% of bsdETH market cap serves as cushion providing a degree of over-collateralization above the floor. Underlying ETH custody rests with the LST issuers (Coinbase, Lido node operators, and Origin Protocol respectively) with no bank-trust-style legal segregation at any layer.

bsdETH recorded no basket deviation events against ETH peg since February 2024 deployment, and on-chain redemption has been uninterrupted throughout. Annualized price volatility against ETH averages approximately 30%. Secondary daily market volume averages below $1M over trailing 30 days.

A $10M Immunefi bug bounty is active across core contracts and LST collateral plugins. No security incident has affected bsdETH or Reserve Protocol since the October 2022 mainnet launch. Basket rebalancing is executed through on-chain governance with Dutch auction settlement. Approximately 90% of staking yield accrues to bsdETH holders and 10% to staked RSR. In a collateral default event, staked RSR is mechanistically seized and auctioned on-chain without requiring a governance vote; unstaking carries a mandatory 14-day delay.
